detailed_description: The JSON to Protocol Buffers converter creates a simple proto3 snippet from pasted JSON in the browser. You can set the root message name and package name, paste JSON, click Convert, and copy the generated output. The converter parses JSON with JSON.parse, uses the root object or the first array item, assigns sequential field numbers, converts field names to snake_case, creates nested messages for nested objects and arrays of objects, and maps basic values to proto scalar types such as int32, int64, double, bool, and string. Date-like strings may be typed as google.protobuf.Timestamp, but the tool does not provide advanced schema controls, map detection, oneof inference, reserved ranges, naming-style options, comments with origin paths, .proto download, identifier validation, or protoc compatibility guarantees.
usage_steps: Enter the root message name and package name.
Paste a JSON object, or an array whose first item represents the message shape.
Click Convert to generate a proto3 snippet.
Review the inferred scalar, repeated, and nested message fields.
Copy the generated output when it is useful as a starting point.
usage_examples: Generate a starter proto3 message from a small JSON API response sample.
Create nested message fields from representative object data before manual cleanup.
Turn an array of similar objects into repeated fields based on the first item.
Copy a quick proto draft and review field types and numbering manually.
